payload.stem: A $15\text{ kg}$ box rests on a horizontal conveyor belt. The belt speeds up from rest with a constant acceleration of $1.5\text{ m/s}^2$, and the box does not slip on the belt. The coefficient of static friction between the box and the belt is $0.6$. What is the magnitude of the friction force that the belt exerts on the box?

options.why: Uses the weight of the box $mg$ as the friction force.

The belt's friction is the only horizontal force on the box and the box accelerates with the belt, so $f=ma=(15)(1.5)=22.5\text{ N}$. It is below the maximum static friction $88.2\text{ N}$, so the box does not slip.
Multiplies the coefficient of friction by the acceleration and the mass, $\mu_s ma$.
Divides the acceleration by the mass instead of multiplying.
